title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Chip chop on the Nasdaq as Nvidia week paddles out
conditions.summary: Nasdaq futures are down close to 1% as chip and AI stocks slide ahead of Nvidia's results, while the Dow holds flat. Yields are higher and markets now price a December Fed hike.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: Early quotes (about 4:00-4:45 AM CT, thin trade): S&P 500 futures -0.3% to -0.4%, Nasdaq-100 futures -0.9% to -1.0%, Dow futures roughly flat, Russell 2000 futures -0.4% to -0.5%.
The 10-year Treasury yield is up about 5 basis points near 5.15%; the 2-year eased slightly after its biggest weekly jump in over two years.
WTI crude is near $88.40, gold near $3,873 and bitcoin near $64,500, all modestly lower; VIX is around 20.
Asia: Nikkei -2.4% after Japan's Q3 GDP contracted; Shanghai -0.9% after weak Chinese October data; Hang Seng +0.5%.
Europe is mixed in early trade. A dollar index reading was not available in the sources checked.
Last week the S&P 500, Nasdaq and Dow each gained more than 2%.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: 7:30 AM CT: Empire State manufacturing (Nov), forecasts about 17.6 to 19 vs. 25.5 prior.
Fed speakers: NY Fed's Williams around 8:05 AM CT and Chair Kevin Warsh around 11:00 AM CT.
Futures now fully price a Fed rate hike in December after last week's hotter-than-expected inflation data.
Geopolitics: Iran struck a US base in Bahrain on Sunday, but the IEA says oil supply now exceeds demand.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Before the open: Baidu, Tyson Foods and Aramark report today.
After the close: AECOM and Powell Industries.
Nvidia reports Tuesday after the close; consensus is about $2.47 adjusted EPS on roughly $109 billion in revenue.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: NVDA (Nvidia): -2.2% — first report since its CEO stepped down is due Tuesday; reports say allies are pushing to bring Jensen Huang back.
INTC (Intel): down about 3.5-5% — chip selloff plus a proposed shareholder class action.
AMD, AVGO, MU (AMD, Broadcom, Micron): down about 3.5-5% — broad chip and AI selloff, echoing weakness in SK Hynix and Samsung.
CRWV, NBIS (CoreWeave, Nebius): about -5.4% and -5.5% — AI infrastructure names under pressure.
DELL, HPQ (Dell, HP): about -5.1%; SMCI (Super Micro): -3.8% — AI hardware selling.
MSTR (Strategy): about -8% — bitcoin slid toward $64,000, weighing on crypto-linked stocks.
NVO (Novo Nordisk): about +3% — strong Phase 3 weight-loss data for CagriSema.

sections.title: Business News
items: Anthropic is expected to begin trading on Nasdaq Thursday, Nov. 19, at a valuation of up to about $1.4 trillion, possibly the largest IPO on record.
Nvidia's leadership turmoil continues: CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, and the FT reports a campaign to reinstate Jensen Huang.
Huang's exit has revived the US chip-export debate ahead of a planned Trump-Xi meeting this week.
Middle East tensions rose after an Iranian strike on a US helicopter base in Bahrain and tanker incidents near Hormuz.
Take-Two has confirmed Grand Theft Auto VI launches this Thursday, Nov. 19.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 7:30 AM CT Empire State survey and the 10-year yield near 5.15%.
11:00 AM CT Fed Chair Warsh remarks for any hint on the size of a December hike.
Whether chip stocks and Nasdaq futures stabilize ahead of Nvidia's Tuesday report.

sections.title: Earnings This Week
items: Mon: Baidu (BIDU), Tyson Foods (TSN), before open — China demand and AI; protein costs.
Tue: Home Depot (HD), before open — big-ticket project demand with high borrowing costs.
Tue: Walt Disney (DIS), before open — parks and streaming.
Tue: Nvidia (NVDA), after close — first report since Huang's exit; guidance and the interim CEO's call.
Wed: Target (TGT), Lowe's (LOW), TJX (TJX), before open — consumer spending under higher energy prices.
Wed: Palo Alto Networks (PANW), after close — cybersecurity demand.
Thu: Walmart (WMT), before open — how shoppers respond to higher prices.
Thu: Alibaba (BABA) — timing to be confirmed; China consumer and cloud.
Thu: Intuit (INTU), Ross Stores (ROST), after close — small business and off-price retail.

sections.title: Economic Calendar This Week
items: Mon 7:30 AM CT: Empire State manufacturing — forecast about 17.6-19 (prior 25.5); Fed Chair Warsh speaks ~11:00 AM CT.
Tue 7:30 AM CT: Retail sales (Oct) — consensus +0.2% m/m, ex-autos +0.4%; import prices +0.7%.
Tue 8:15 AM CT: Industrial production — consensus +0.1%; 9:00 AM NAHB housing index — 29.
Wed 7:30 AM CT: Housing starts — 1.25M; building permits — 1.38M.
Wed 1:00 PM CT: FOMC minutes from the Oct. 27-28 meeting.
Thu 7:30 AM CT: Jobless claims — 199K; Philly Fed — 19.2. Anthropic expected to debut on Nasdaq.
Fri 9:00 AM CT: UMich consumer sentiment (final) — 52.1.
Busy Fed week: Williams, Waller, Musalem, Hammack, Goolsbee, Barr and others speak; markets debate a 25 vs. 50 bp December hike.
Friday, Nov. 20 is the third Friday of the month (likely monthly options expiration).

Wednesday has housing starts at seven thirty and the Fed minutes at one P M Central. Thursday has jobless claims and the Philly Fed survey at seven thirty, plus the Anthropic debut.
